artifacts.summary: Confirms the disproven subagent-barrier claim already corrected in mcp-server-ownership.md, pinpoints docs-README.md line 78 as the sole in-scope stale claim, reproduces live MCP fan-out (6 sessions x 3 procs, ~976MB VmSwap-aware) and both zombie classes (7 sd_* + 1 lake <defunct>) with real PIDs, and recommends extending claude-refresh.sh with two new report-only pass functions following the task-159 two-pass precedent.

memory_candidates.content: context/patterns/mcp-server-ownership.md already contains the corrected workspace-trust framing for MCP subagent access (sections 'Workspace trust' and 'The session-start snapshot trap') — it is not itself in need of correction; only docs/docs-README.md's older categorical 'subagents cannot access project-scoped MCP servers' claim lags behind it. When auditing for this claim repo-wide, .opencode/docs/README.md and .opencode/extensions/core/docs/README.md carry the identical stale wording but are a separate system's docs, out of scope for agent-system/extensions/core/ edits.

claude-refresh.sh's established multi-pass pattern (set by the Lean LSP reclamation task): main() calls independent run_*_pass("$FORCE" "$DRY_RUN") functions unconditionally in sequence, each taking its own ps snapshot, reusing get_vmswap_kb/format_memory/get_process_age/is_system_slice_cgroup/is_owned_by_current_uid as shared helpers, and calling terminate_pid only if the pass is actually destructive. A report-only pass should never call terminate_pid/kill at all — grep-verifiable, and produces byte-identical --dry-run/--force output modulo the [DRY RUN] banner, which is the mechanical proof of non-destructiveness.
